summary: Spotsylvania County, VA 110-foot Aermotor tower moved from Prince William Forest Park to Partlow in 1961; NHLR-registered 2017; standing, state-administered, access restricted.

facts.design: 110-foot Aermotor tower with 7'x7' cab (NHLR); the earlier tower at Prince William Forest Park is described as wooden (FFLOS)

access.note: State-administered site. The 2019 NHLR visit report notes security cameras, and the visitor did not approach the base. No public visiting arrangement found.

events.note: FFLOS register gives 1942 as the build year for the tower at Prince William Forest Park; its description says it was erected at the beginning of WWII
Moved from Prince William Forest Park and erected at Partlow in October 1961 (newspaper: 13 forestry staff; NHLR: 13 locals)
NHLR visit report dated August 9, 2019: rust, missing window glass seen in aerial image, cell tower antennas and dishes, not staffed

corrections.proposed: 1942 built at Prince William Forest Park; 1961 relocated to Partlow
corrections.why: The NHLR 1961 'Built' date is for the erection at Partlow. The FFLOS register gives 1942 as the build year, and the 1961 newspaper says the tower had been at the park since early in WWII.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS calls the Prince William Forest Park tower wooden, while NHLR calls the same tower, once moved to Partlow, a 110-foot Aermotor. The story reports both descriptions and does not settle the construction.
FFLOS build field says 1942, its description says the beginning of WWII, and the 1961 newspaper says since early in the war. The story gives the register's 1942 and the wartime wording together.

notes_for_editor: The brief's '1961 built' is the NHLR erection date at Partlow; the tower stood at Prince William Forest Park from early in WWII (FFLOS build year 1942). FFLOS calls the earlier tower wooden while NHLR calls it an Aermotor; unresolved. The newest source is the NHLR visit report of August 9, 2019; no later condition or staffing data was found. The site has security cameras and cell antennas, so the story does not suggest approaching the base. Record elevation 126.8 m matches NHLR 416 ft (127 m). Staffing dates are unknown.
